groups.title: In the streets
groups.desc: The city's own fair fills the last ten days of October, and the castanyada and Tots Sants close it.

items.name: The fair and the fire: Fires de Sant Narcís
items.teaser: Ten days of rides, concerts and a correfoc in the old town, Friday 23 October to Sunday 1 November
items.story: Girona's own fair opens on Friday 23 October and runs to Sunday 1 November, with about 200 events on the programme. The rides go up in the Devesa, the plane-tree park beside the Ter, and the main concerts play each night at La Copa, opening with Miki Núñez at 22:30 on the first Friday. On Saturday 24 at 22:30 the devils' correfoc runs sparks through the Plaça del Vi; the castellers build human towers on Sunday 25 at 11:30. Monday 26 has a quiet fair from 17:00 to 20:00, with rides and music turned down. The closing fireworks go up on Sunday 1 November at 20:00.
items.why: Stand well back in the Plaça del Vi on Saturday night, in cotton, with the sleeves down.
facts: Fri 23 Oct to Sun 1 Nov 2026; correfoc Sat 24, 22:30; fireworks Sun 1 Nov, 20:00
Rides in the Devesa park; concerts at La Copa; correfoc in the Plaça del Vi

items.name: The saint's day and the flies
items.teaser: Thursday 29 October is Sant Narcís: a city holiday, havaneres on the cathedral steps, sardanes in the squares
items.story: Narcís is Girona's patron, and the story told about him is the reason for the fly emblems seen all over town in late October: during a siege, flies poured out of the saint's tomb and drove off the attackers. It is a legend, not history; the fair opens with a hanging of flies in the Plaça de l'Assumpció. His day, Thursday 29 October, is a holiday in Girona and the fullest day of the programme, with havaneres sung on the steps below the cathedral. Through the fair the sardana groups compete in the squares: the 2025 programme counted the 84th contest of colles sardanistes.
items.why: Spend the 29th in the Barri Vell: shops close, the squares fill, and the cathedral steps become a stage.
facts: Thu 29 Oct 2026, the feast day and a Girona holiday

items.name: Chestnut smoke and an earlier dusk
items.teaser: Clocks go back on Sunday 25 October; the castanyada falls on Saturday 31, before the Tots Sants holiday
items.story: Two small changes alter the week of the fair. On Sunday 25 October Spain goes back to winter time, so evenings at the fair are dark by tea time and the light comes back earlier in the morning. Then comes the castanyada, on the evening of Saturday 31 October. Families eat roasted chestnuts, sweet potatoes and panellets with a glass of moscatell, and the castanyeres sell hot chestnuts in paper cones from street stalls. Sunday 1 November, Tots Sants, is a public holiday and the day of family visits to the cemeteries, and it closes the fair with the fireworks.
items.why: Buy a cone of chestnuts from a street stall on the walk to the fireworks on the 1st.
facts: Clocks back Sun 25 Oct; castanyada Sat 31 Oct; Tots Sants holiday Sun 1 Nov 2026

groups.title: In the hills and the woods
groups.desc: The Garrotxa beeches colour, the Gavarres give their mushrooms, and the Empordà olives are picked.

items.name: The beeches of the Fageda d'en Jordà turn
items.teaser: The beech wood on a lava flow near Olot colours from late October to mid-November; come early, parking fills
items.story: The Fageda d'en Jordà is a beech forest growing flat on an old lava flow in the Garrotxa volcanic park, about an hour north-west of Girona. Beeches usually grow in the mountains; here they stand on low ground. Guides put the colour change between late October and mid-November, the leaves going from yellow to copper and rust. The first crowds tend to arrive on the last weekend of October, with queues on the road and the paid car parks full. The usual start is the Can Serra information centre on the Olot to Santa Pau road, and the Joan Maragall trail is the short, easy loop.
items.why: Go on a weekday morning in the first half of November, when the colour is deepest.
facts: Late Oct to mid-Nov is the usual colour window; no 2026 forecast published

The walk is free; parking is paid

items.name: Mushrooms from the Gavarres at Llagostera
items.teaser: Llagostera's mushroom fair and restaurant menus use the Gavarres woods; the 2026 date is still unconfirmed
items.story: The Gavarres, the low wooded hills between Girona and the coast, are the town's mushroom country, and Llagostera, about twenty minutes south of the city, has built an autumn around them since 2003. The Fira del Bolet has a market of autumn produce, a contest and display of specimens picked in the Gavarres, and cooking demonstrations; an earlier edition drew more than 10,000 people. Alongside it the town's restaurants run La Cuina del Bolet, a set of mushroom menus, which in 2025 ran from 12 to 27 October. Listings for 2026 say only October, with one undated hint of 25 October, so check with the town before driving out.
items.why: Book a mushroom menu in Llagostera rather than picking: identification is for experts.
facts: Usually mid to late October (menus 12-27 Oct in 2025); 2026 dates not confirmed

items.name: Olives coming off the Empordà trees
items.teaser: Argudell olives are being picked; the new Empordà oil is shown at the Mercat del Lleó in December
items.story: The Empordà's own olive is the argudell, the main variety of the DOP Oli de l'Empordà and the one that gives the oil its green, slightly bitter edge. Picking starts as autumn sets in, and by mid-October markets in the region were already selling oil on the edge of the new harvest. Spain's first national estimate for 2026-27, given on 1 October, is 1.6 million tonnes, up 23 percent, but it forecasts a smaller crop for Catalonia. The new oil of the Empordà is presented each December in Girona at the Mercat del Lleó; in 2024 that was on 14 December. The 2026 date is not yet out.
items.why: Ask at the mill shops in December for the first-pressed argudell and use it raw.
facts: Harvest from autumn into winter; new-oil presentation usually mid-December (14 Dec in 2024)

groups.title: On the plate
groups.desc: A cork-workers' stew on the coast, the sweets of All Saints and a farm breakfast as the mornings cool.

items.name: Es Niu, the cork-workers' stew, in Palafrugell
items.teaser: Palafrugell's restaurants cook the old niu from 16 October to 13 December 2026
items.story: Before tourism, Palafrugell lived from cork, and the niu was a dish of its workers' tables: a slow, dark stew built on salt-cod tripe and cuttlefish, cooked for hours. The town's campaign brings it back each autumn in a group of local restaurants, alongside tastings and popular events. In 2026 Es Niu runs from 16 October to 13 December, according to the Surt de Casa listing; the 2025 edition ran from 17 October to 14 December. Palafrugell is about forty minutes east of Girona by road, an easy lunch on the way back to a boat at Palamós or Calella.
items.why: Phone ahead: the town hall tells diners to confirm with each restaurant before going.
facts: 16 Oct to 13 Dec 2026 (one listing; not yet confirmed by the town hall)

items.name: Panellets and moscatell for Tots Sants
items.teaser: Almond and pine-nut panellets fill the pastry windows for the castanyada; eat them with sweet moscatell
items.story: In the last days of October every pastisseria in Girona puts out trays of panellets, small marzipan sweets of ground almond and sugar, the best known rolled in pine nuts, others in coconut, coffee or cocoa. They belong to the castanyada on 31 October and Tots Sants on 1 November, alongside roasted chestnuts and sweet potatoes, and the traditional drink with them is moscatell, a sweet wine. The pine-nut kind costs most because of the nuts. After 1 November they disappear from the windows for another year, so this is the fortnight.
items.why: Order a mixed tray from a city pastry shop for the guests' coffee on the 31st.
facts: Last week of October to 1 November

items.name: A fork breakfast at Ca l'Àngel
items.teaser: Meatballs with wild mushrooms at six in the morning, and a xuixo flambéed with ratafia, 15 minutes north
items.story: Ca l'Àngel is a roadside bar on the Banyoles to Figueres road, opened in 1978 and now run by the founders' children. Its trade is the esmorzar de forquilla, the knife-and-fork breakfast of the Catalan countryside, and the pots come out at six: cap i pota, botifarra with beans, meatballs with wild mushrooms. In January 2025 ElNacional.cat named it the best fork breakfast in the Pla de l'Estany. The finish is Girona's xuixo, warmed on the grill and flambéed with ratafia. As the mornings turn cold after the clocks change, this is the season for it.
items.why: Go on the way to the Fageda or Besalú, and call ahead on 972 57 50 99.
facts: Mon-Fri 6:00-16:30, Sat 6:00-12:00; closed Sundays and holidays

Any change, up or down, moves the booking lines the next morning. Esperit Roca is also on holiday from 3 to 11 November.

items.name: Ratafia in Besalú, late November
items.teaser: Besalú's ratafia fair and contest usually falls on the last weekend of November; 2026 date not yet out
items.story: Ratafia is the Garrotxa's walnut liqueur, made from green walnuts picked around Sant Joan and steeped with herbs and spices for months. Besalú, the walled medieval town with the fortified bridge half an hour north of Girona, has held a fair for it for more than three decades. In 2025 the 32nd edition ran on 29 and 30 November, with the contest on the Saturday evening and the winner presented on Sunday; in 2024 it fell on 30 November and 1 December. Entry is free and the town hall organises it. The 2026 fair has not been announced.
items.why: Taste several house ratafias at the stalls before buying a bottle for the bar.
facts: Usually the last weekend of November (29-30 Nov in 2025); 2026 not yet announced

items.name: Temps de Flors
items.teaser: Courtyards, steps and churches of the old town dressed in flowers for about a week in mid-May
items.story: For about a week each May, Girona opens the courtyards of its old houses, its monuments and its stairways to installations of flowers and plants, many by local groups and designers, and the Barri Vell becomes one long route between them. The 2026 edition, the 71st, ran from 9 to 17 May. The 2027 dates had not been announced when this was checked. It is the city's busiest stretch of the spring, and the narrow streets around the cathedral fill from mid-morning, so weekdays and early hours are the times to go.
items.why: Walk the cathedral steps before ten on a weekday.
facts: Usually mid-May (9-17 May in 2026); 2027 dates not yet published

items.name: Sant Jordi
items.teaser: 23 April: bookstalls and roses along the Rambla and through the old town; in 2027 it falls on a Friday
items.story: Sant Jordi, the patron of Catalonia, is the day for giving a book and a rose. In Girona the stalls of booksellers and florists line the Rambla de la Llibertat and spread through the Barri Vell, open from 9:00 to 21:00, and authors sign at the tables through the day. It is a working day, not a holiday, so the crowd thickens at lunch and after work. In 2027, 23 April is a Friday. Building works have moved stalls in past years, so check the layout a few days before.
items.why: Buy the rose from a stall run by a school or a charity.

items.name: Festival Strenes
items.teaser: Girona's spring music festival, more than 30 shows in Girona and Salt from late March into early May
items.story: Strenes is the city's spring music festival, and it runs long: not a weekend but five or six weeks of concerts spread across Girona and neighbouring Salt. The 14th edition in 2026 put on more than 30 shows from 27 March to 3 May; the 2025 edition ran from 26 March to 4 May, so the pattern is steady. That stretch takes in Sant Jordi and often brushes the start of Temps de Flors, which makes it easy to fold a concert into a spring visit. The 2027 programme had not been announced when checked.

items.name: Sant Joan
items.teaser: The night of 23 June: the Flame of the Canigó arrives, bonfires are lit and coca is eaten until late
items.story: The eve of Sant Joan, the night of 23 to 24 June, is the shortest night's party across Catalonia. The Flama del Canigó, a flame carried down from the mountain in French Catalonia, is passed from town to town and lights the bonfires; a manifesto is read and the coca de Sant Joan, a flat sweet bread with candied fruit, is shared. On the Girona coast, Begur, Tossa, Blanes and L'Estartit all hold revetlles with fire, music and dancing. In 2027 the 23rd is a Wednesday, and the 24th is a public holiday in Catalonia.
items.why: Anchor off a town with a beach bonfire and watch from the water.
facts: Night of 23 June every year (Wed 23 June 2027)

items.name: Cantada d'Havaneres, Calella de Palafrugell
items.teaser: First Saturday of July, havaneres on the beach at Port Bo; the 2026 edition was called off by a forest fire
items.story: Havaneres are the songs Catalan sailors brought home from Cuba, and the sing-song on the beach at Port Bo in Calella de Palafrugell is the most famous night for them. It is held on the first Saturday of July, with cremat, burnt rum, passed round afterwards. In 2026 the 59th edition, set for 4 July, was cancelled on the day on the advice of the emergency services because of a forest fire; it had been suspended only once before, in 2020. The first Saturday of July 2027 is the 3rd.
items.why: Come by tender and watch from the water, as many boats do.
facts: First Saturday of July (Sat 3 July 2027 if the pattern holds)

items.name: Fires de Sant Narcís
items.teaser: Girona's ten-day fair around its patron's day, 29 October: Devesa rides, sardanes, correfoc, fireworks
items.story: Each autumn Girona builds ten days of festivities around its patron Sant Narcís, whose feast is 29 October. The Devesa park takes the funfair, the squares hold sardana contests and havaneres, the devils run a correfoc through the old town and fireworks close it. In 2025 the fair ran from 24 October to 2 November; in 2026 it is 23 October to 1 November. The 2027 dates were not out when checked, but the shape stays the same: about ten days spanning the 29th.
items.why: Book restaurant tables for the 29th weeks ahead.

items.name: Fira de la Ratafia de Besalú
items.teaser: Late November or early December: Besalú's free fair and contest for the walnut liqueur of the Garrotxa
items.story: Besalú, the medieval town on the Fluvià with its fortified bridge, gives one weekend at the end of autumn to ratafia, the dark liqueur of green walnuts and herbs made in farmhouses across the Garrotxa. Makers set out stalls, and a contest picks the year's best on the Saturday evening. The fair has run for more than thirty years: the 32nd edition was on 29 and 30 November 2025, the 31st on 30 November and 1 December 2024.
items.why: Combine it with lunch in Besalú and a walk over the bridge.

items.name: La Castanyada
items.teaser: 31 October: roasted chestnuts, sweet potatoes, panellets and moscatell, the eve of the Tots Sants holiday
items.story: The castanyada is the Catalan autumn feast of All Saints' eve. Chestnut sellers set up braziers in the streets, and at home the table has roasted chestnuts, baked sweet potatoes, panellets and candied fruit, washed down with moscatell. It used to be held on Tots Sants itself, 1 November, and has shifted to the evening before. The next day is a public holiday, when families visit the graves of their dead. In 2027, 31 October is a Sunday and 1 November a Monday.
items.why: Have panellets with the coffee and a chilled moscatell.
facts: 31 October, eve of the 1 November holiday
